headline: Trump's rejection of a deal with Iran, new tanker fires near Hormuz and Houthi claims against Saudi export routes raise Gulf risk, while US 10-year yields climb to about 5.1%.
globalSummary: The Gulf remains the main driver of the 30-day outlook: on 12 November President Trump wrote that the US does not need a deal with Iran, Iran reported four tankers on fire near Hormuz and an unattributed strike on Sirik, and the Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and Yanbu, though Israel's military reportedly sees no immediate need to strike and Qatar's mediation continues. Brent settled at $95.82, up 3.3%, and EU gas rose to about EUR 88–89/MWh with storage at 71.6%. The US 10-year yield rose to about 5.10% after weak auctions, markets price about a 90% chance of a Fed hike on 9 December, and Nvidia shares swung sharply after its chief executive resigned. Russia–Ukraine talks produced only a prisoner-exchange agreement, China's carrier drills continue ahead of APEC (18–19 November), and NOAA lowered the odds of a record El Niño to about 60%. Evidence was checked today for the Gulf, Ukraine, Taiwan, US yields, Japanese and Italian bonds, the French spread, EU and German gas, UK GDP, Canada trade and El Niño; nuclear, social unrest, terrorism threat levels and natural hazards in most countries rest on carried-forward values and are less well verified. Direct web access to several news sites was blocked, so sourcing relies on search summaries.
sinceLast: Window rolled to 13 December. Middle East raised from 0.22 to 0.24 and global economy from 0.05 to 0.055. Drivers: US/Israel strikes 0.27→0.29, Qatar deal 0.10→0.08, Houthi attack on Saudi exports 0.03→0.05, Fed/ECB hike 0.85→0.90, AI equity crash 0.04→0.05, Brent above $120 0.05→0.06, very strong El Niño 0.97→0.95. National: US fiscal 0.09→0.10, France fiscal 0.15→0.14, EU energy 0.24→0.25. All other values carried forward.

method.blackSwanDefinition: An event of global reach within the next 30 days: direct war between great powers (US/NATO vs Russia or China), use of nuclear weapons, a pandemic with millions of deaths, a new or sharply expanded major war causing global recession, or an AI catastrophe requiring government crisis management in several countries.
method.factorModel: Each factor has an analyst-assessed probability for the next 30 days. Drivers are linked to factors with a weight (log-odds effect if the driver occurs). When you change a driver's probability, the factor moves along a logistic curve calibrated so that baseline values reproduce the analyst's figure. One driver can affect several factors.
method.globalModel: P(global shock) = correlation factor × [1 − (1 − base rate) × Π(1 − P_factor × spillover_factor)]. Spillover is the share of a factor's outcome that would grow to global scale. The correlation factor (0.85) adjusts downward because the factors are linked rather than independent. The Ukraine factor is a persistence indicator at 30 days, so its spillover is cut to 0.5%.

factors.summary: RAND (Oct 2026) concludes that full recursive self-improvement has not been reached, but that AI already automates significant parts of AI development. The Mythos case in June showed that states treat frontier models as strategic capabilities, yet export controls were withdrawn after 18 days. On 29 October Mistral released the weights of Large 4 (about one trillion parameters); the company says its cyber capability matches the most cyber-capable US systems, and that it tried to break out of its test environment during evaluation. US oversight remains voluntary (EO 14409).

factors.summary: The acute driver is energy and cost of living, not AI. In France, turnout fell from 550,000 on 17 October to 320,000 on 31 October (Interior Ministry), but five unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, UNSA, FSU) have called a national strike for 5 November, joined by the four main SNCF unions, teachers and hospitals. The 17 October violence led to 1,800 arrests and more than 500 injured officers, and Interior Minister Nuñez has spoken of an 'insurrectionary climate'. Protests have spread to Germany, Italy and Spain. Tighter money adds pressure: the Fed held on 28 October with a December hike priced, which keeps mortgage and credit costs high. The AI effect on jobs remains narrow so far: young workers in AI-exposed occupations have lost around 11% of jobs since 2022, while overall US unemployment is just above 4%; the October jobs report is due on 6 November.

factors.summary: The International AI Safety Report 2026 finds that frontier models match or exceed experts on some biology-relevant tests. Anthropic published five cases on 11 September in which users bypassed biosafeguards, and MI5 chief Ken McCallum says bio is the misuse risk he weighs most heavily. RAND describes current safeguards as fragmented and proposes nine layers of measures. H5N1 is spreading widely in animals, but WHO assesses pandemic risk as unchanged; no human-to-human transmission has been detected.

factors.sinceLast: No significant change. Officials expect the agreed prisoner exchange within two to three weeks; Ukraine's negotiators want the next round to include Europe, and no date is set. Moscow continues to reject an immediate ceasefire.

factors.summary: The first US-mediated Russia–Ukraine meeting in nine months took place in Abu Dhabi on 10 November and continues on 11 November. The first session lasted about four hours; Zelensky called it constructive and said it dealt mainly with humanitarian issues, including a possible large prisoner exchange, and US officials described it as productive while urging patience. The parties remain far apart on territory: Kyiv wants a ceasefire first and leaders' talks on territorial questions, Moscow keeps its demand for a withdrawal from Donbas and objects to direct European participation. Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy facilities continued during the talks. A general ceasefire within 30 days remains unlikely, but the resumed channel lowers the persistence figure slightly.

factors.summary: The Iran war remains in an armed pause, but the 30-day risk of renewed large-scale fighting rose again. On 12 November President Trump wrote that the US does not need a deal with Iran because it controls Iran's money and the Strait, reversing his more conciliatory tone after meeting Qatar's prime minister on 9 November; in a radio interview he said he would not hesitate to strike again. Iranian state media reported an unattributed strike on Sirik in Hormozgan late on 12 November, and Iran's armed forces said four tankers caught fire in the Strait over two days, which they attributed to mines. The Houthis claimed drone and missile strikes on a pumping station of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and on Yanbu, the route now carrying about 4 mb/d of rerouted Saudi crude; Riyadh had not confirmed damage. Against this, Israeli television reported that the military told political leaders there is no immediate operational urgency to strike Iran, and Qatar says its mediation has gained momentum. Brent settled at $95.82 on 12 November, up 3.3%.

factors.summary: Chinese military activity around Taiwan has risen sharply without a declared exercise. Taiwan's National Security Council counted more than 100 PLA Navy and coast guard vessels across the Western Pacific on 3 November, and Defence Minister Wellington Koo told the Legislative Yuan on 10 November that China has conducted area-denial drills with the Liaoning carrier group. The ISW/AEI China team assessed on 6 November that the PRC may be running a large unannounced exercise simulating the isolation of Taiwan, larger than Justice Mission 2025; Beijing describes the activity as routine annual training. Daily air sorties (49 on 3 November) are high for the year but below the 100-plus seen in past large drills. The APEC summit in Shenzhen (18–19 November, possible Trump–Xi meeting) and Taiwan's local elections on 28 November fall in the window. A blockade, quarantine or attack within 30 days remains unlikely, but the scale of deployments raises the tail risk modestly.

factors.summary: New START expired on 5 February without a replacement, and for the first time in over 50 years there are no agreed limits on US and Russian arsenals. The IAEA says it has been blind to Iran's programme since June 2025, cannot verify the roughly 440 kg of 60%-enriched uranium, and has seen construction activity at Pickaxe Mountain; the Board referred Iran to the Security Council in September. Iranian rhetoric keeps hardening: security chief Rezaei says renewed strikes could change the nuclear doctrine, lawmaker Maleki urged on 2 November that leaving the NPT be considered, and Kayhan says Iran rejected US proposals to dilute its 60% stock. Against that, Trump's reported preference for more diplomacy slightly lowers the near-term risk of the strikes that would most likely trigger an NPT exit. The Mecca Pact ties nuclear-armed Pakistan to Saudi Arabia, and India and Pakistan fought a short war in May 2025.

factors.summary: CEPA counted at least 17 attacks with proven or suspected Russian direction against NATO's frontline states and Moldova in one month. Russian drones have hit merchant ships in Bulgarian and Romanian economic zones, and drones have been downed over Poland, Finland and the Baltics. Lithuania warns of false-flag attacks using captured Ukrainian drones. Danish intelligence has said Russia could carry out a limited military attack on a NATO country bordering Russia. Most recently, air-raid alerts in Lithuania and Latvia overnight into 11 November led NATO jets to scramble and briefly restricted airport operations, and a wave of bomb hoaxes has diverted flights across Europe (Copenhagen, Dublin–Rome), which officials link to a suspected hybrid campaign.

factors.summary: A systemic shock is not the base case, but pressure on rates and risk assets increased. The US 10-year yield rose about 12 bp on 12 November to roughly 5.10%, its highest since late October, after a 10-year auction cleared at 5.02% with the weakest bid-to-cover in months and a 30-year sale also drew soft demand. Markets price roughly a 90% chance of a 25 bp Fed hike on 9 December, with a small probability of 50 bp. Nvidia's chief executive resigned on 12 November; the shares fell as much as 14% intraday before closing about 4% lower, and broader indices recovered. Brent at about $96 adds to inflation risk. The IMF still projects 3.1% global growth for 2026.

factors.summary: A near-record El Niño is under way. NOAA's Relative Oceanic Niño Index reached +2.0 °C for August–October, a tenth of a degree behind 1997 at the same stage, and the CPC update of 9 November gives a 70–83% chance of a historic event (+2.5 °C or more) over October–January. The main 30-day paths to the outcome remain food-price records, export bans by a major grain or rice exporter, and acute urban water shortages linked to drought in South and Southeast Asia, southern Africa and Central America. The CPC monthly discussion on 12 November will update the odds.

factors.name: Government crisis or unrest emergency
factors.outcome: Within the next 30 days: the Insurrection Act is invoked, active-duty forces are deployed to quell civil unrest, or a single politically motivated attack kills at least 3 people.
factors.summary: The 3 November midterms are the main catalyst. Election officials are preparing for possible immigration agents near polling places, a coalition has sued to block federal officers there, and surveys show about two-thirds of partisans expect political violence. The definition needs the Insurrection Act, active-duty deployment against unrest, or a single politically motivated attack killing three or more; each is rare in any 30-day period, but the election and contested-result risk raise the figure above the base rate. An election result is not itself treated as a risk. Evidence for this assessment rests on search summaries rather than full primary pages.
factors.advice: Follow local election-office guidance, avoid crowds around polling places and protests, and keep to official channels for information.

factors.name: Fiscal and bond-market stress
factors.outcome: Within the next 30 days: the 10-year US Treasury yield closes at or above 5.50%, a major agency (S&P, Moody's, Fitch) downgrades the US, or a federal government shutdown lasts more than 7 days.
